sentences.text: The genus Foskeia contains only one known species, F. pelendonum, represented by fossils of multiple individuals at different growth stages.
Dieudonné and colleagues reported finding at least five individuals of a small, gracile ornithopod about 0.5 meters long in 2016.
New cranial elements found later and analyzed with μCT scanning led to the formal description of the genus and species in 2026.
The name Foskeia comes from Ancient Greek words meaning 'light' and 'to forage', referencing the animal's small size and likely herbivory.
The species name pelendonum honors the Pelendones, a Celtiberian tribe from near the fossil site.
Juvenile Foskeia started life as quadrupeds but transitioned to bipedalism at an early stage of growth.
The largest known individual was a late subadult, suggesting Foskeia was one of the smallest ornithopods.
The shift from quadrupedal to bipedal locomotion in Foskeia is consistent with patterns seen in other early rhabdodontomorphs.
In 2026, Dieudonné and colleagues placed Foskeia in a new subclade called Rhabdodontia within Rhabdodontomorpha.
Phylogenetic analysis places Foskeia as the sister taxon to traditional Rhabdodontidae, diverging after Muttaburrasaurus and Fostoria.
Recent analyses place the rhabdodontomorph clade in a more advanced position at the base of Ankylopollexia.
Foskeia belongs to the class Sauropsida.
Foskeia is classified within the superorder Dinosauria.
Foskeia is an ornithischian dinosaur.
Foskeia is classified within the infraorder Ornithopoda.
Foskeia lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Barremian to Aptian stages.
The type locality for Foskeia is the Castrillo de la Reina Formation.
Foskeia fossils have been found in Spain.
Foskeia lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
Researchers define the new clade Rhabdodontia as a restricted group of European rhabdodontomorphs including Foskeia and rhabdodontids.
The current phylogenetic placement of rhabdodontomorphs is considered provisional pending the addition of more saurischian data.
